# 10 — Deployments and quote assets

<!-- generated:status-banner -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

> **RC6 is LIVE AND OPEN ON THREE CHAINS.** RC6 is deployed and PUBLIC on Ethereum (1), Base (8453) and Robinhood Chain (4663): all three accept ordinary, permissionless creator launches. The factory is the same CREATE2 address on all three. RC6 is NOT deployed on BNB Smart Chain (56), which is deferred, and no date is set for it.
> Public creator launch is **open** on Ethereum (1), Base (8453), Robinhood Chain (4663) and **closed** on the other 1 configured chain.
> See [08 — Status and limitations](08-status.md).

<!-- /generated:status-banner -->

## The RC6 addresses, and where they come from

This page does not restate the address table. The kit carries it as data, generated rather than
typed, and `relics status` prints it:

```
npm run kit:status
```

The record itself is `packages/project-schema/src/deployments.js`, written by
`npm run kit:deployments:sync` from the launchpad's chain profiles. **An address is published only
from a profile that states it was read back off the chain** with `eth_call` / `eth_getCode` — which
is stronger evidence than a deployment flag, because a flag records that a transaction was sent and
a verification records that the code is there now. Nobody hand-types an address into this
repository, and the check runs in CI.

**One factory address, three chains.** `0x25003C3EBC2036CfE9E4037d4e7E6F840a06522E` is the
LaunchpadFactory on Ethereum, on Base and on Robinhood Chain — the deployment is deterministic, so
the same creation inputs land at the same address everywhere. It is an ERC-1967 proxy: the proxy is
the stable address every launch is built against, and the implementation behind it moves under it.

**Robinhood Chain carries one extra entry**, `swapRouter`. Ethereum and Base do not, because their
official Universal Router deployments are canonical there.

**The multi-quote lane is not in this table.** Robinhood is the only chain with a second, non-WETH
quote lane, and the kit does not print its registry and kernel addresses: upstream records them in
a prose note rather than a structured field, and an address parsed out of a sentence is not an
address a creator kit should hand you. `factory.multiQuoteLane()` returns them on chain and is the
authority.

**RC5's platform addresses have been withdrawn from this kit.** Earlier revisions of this page
carried them. RC5's contracts are real, still hold code on the three chains they were deployed to,
and still read `PREPARED` — the state a factory is born in — so they refused an ordinary creator
launch for their whole life and refuse one now. A copyable address you can reach and can never use
is worse than a blank, so the kit prints none of them and says why instead. If you are auditing
history, read them off a block explorer.

## The chains, and what each one quotes in

| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ethereum | 1 | `DEPLOYED` · public launch open | WETH | None. A non-WETH quote is refused by chain id, not by convention. | `etherscan.io` |
| Base | 8453 | `DEPLOYED` · public launch open | WETH | None. A non-WETH quote is refused by chain id, not by convention. | `basescan.org` |
| Robinhood Chain | 4663 | `DEPLOYED` · public launch open | WETH | Multi-quote. Any asset QuoteAssetRegistryV1 currently admits AND leaves enabled: the stablecoin, the Robinhood stock/ETF tokens and the ecosystem token. Governance admits; a bundle can only request. | `robinhoodchain.blockscout.com` |
| BNB Smart Chain | 56 | `PREPARED_NOT_DEPLOYED` · public launch closed | WBNB | None. WBNB is not WETH; never print "WETH" or "ETH" on this chain. | `bscscan.com` |

RC6 is live and open to ordinary creator launches on Ethereum (1), Base (8453) and Robinhood Chain (4663) -- one factory address, the same on all three, because the deployment is deterministic. BNB Smart Chain (56) is configured in the bundle format and the chain profiles and RC6 is not deployed on it; configured is not deployed, and no date is announced. The chains still differ in the quote leg -- Robinhood is the only multi-quote chain, and chain 56 settles in WBNB rather than WETH -- so read the row rather than assuming they match.

## Reading launch state at runtime instead of from a document

Whatever this page says, a program should ask the chain.

```js
import { PLATFORM_DEPLOYMENTS, acceptsPublicLaunches, platformDeployment } from "@relics/project-schema";
```

Two cautions about those exports, both of which matter more than the API shape:

1. **They describe the CURRENT generation's record, and the current generation is named in it.**
   `PLATFORM_DEPLOYMENTS` resolves to the newest generation that is actually deployed, which is RC6;
   `deploymentsFor("RC5")` still exists and answers with an all-`null` table. Read every record as
   "what this kit publishes about that generation", never as "what is on chain" — the second
   question is the chain's to answer.
2. **`acceptsPublicLaunches` is a convenience over a fact you can read yourself.** The authority is
   the factory's own launch-access state. A document — including this one — can be stale; a contract
   read cannot.

`npm run kit:status` prints the same record locally.

## Quote assets: a bundle requests, it never approves

A `.relics` bundle may name the quote asset it wants. The importer resolves that request against the
launchpad's registry on the target chain, and the registry decides.

```json
{
  "market": {
    "chainId": 4663,
    "quoteAsset": {
      "mode": "ADDRESS",
      "address": "0x…",
      "expectedKind": "STOCK_TOKEN"
    }
  }
}
```

**Ethereum and Base admit exactly one quote: the canonical WETH.** A non-WETH quote is refused there
by chain id, not by convention — there is no registry to consult and no request that succeeds.

**BNB Smart Chain admits its wrapped native, WBNB.** Not WETH; not "ETH". See
[06 — Fees and revenue](06-fees-and-revenue.md#which-asset-the-platform-is-paid-in).

**Robinhood Chain is the multi-quote chain.** Any asset the quote registry currently admits *and*
leaves enabled may be named: the wrapped native, the stablecoin, the Robinhood stock and ETF tokens,
and the ecosystem token. The complete official stock/ETF reference is exported from the schema
package rather than reproduced here, because a partial list copied into an app is a list that goes
stale silently:

```js
import { ROBINHOOD_STOCK_TOKEN_COUNT, robinhoodStockTokenBySymbol } from "@relics/project-schema";
```

If you need a selector, import the list and filter it. Do not paste a subset.

### What the quote registry can and cannot do

The registry decides exactly one thing: whether an asset may be **selected as the quote leg of a new
launch**. The selected asset is then written into that project's canonical `PoolKey` and is immutable
for the life of the project.

So disabling an asset blocks **new** launches against it and nothing else. It does not rewrite an
existing `PoolKey` — a `PoolKey` is not writable by anyone — and it does not migrate, drain,
re-route or re-price any existing pool, alter any existing art history, or touch a creator's
entitlements or claims. The property is structural: no function on the registry takes a project id
or a pool id, so there is no expressible call that reaches a launched project.

There is also **no arbitrary-address path**. The admitted-kind vocabulary has no "custom address"
member and the registry has no "admit whatever the caller passes" entrypoint. An unadmitted address
produces exactly one outcome: the launch reverts.

Two roles govern it, deliberately asymmetric. The upgrade authority (the protocol 2-of-3 Safe) admits
assets, updates them, re-enables them and approves conversion routes. A separate guardian holds an
emergency brake **only**: it may disable an asset or a route, and can never enable, admit, widen a
bound, or lower a risk tier. The fast path is strictly de-risking; every re-widening is an act of the
Safe.

`riskTier` is a tier, not a safety label. The protocol never marks an asset "safe" — there is no such
field.

## Quote admission and the WETH route are separate questions

A quote asset can be enabled for new launches before the platform's route from that quote to WETH has
been proven. That is fine and normal: the treasury half of the platform share is claimable in the
quote regardless, and the buy-and-entomb half is allowed to wait, visibly, in its own state.

Do not read "enabled" as "a WETH route exists".

And that is a **different route** from the one a creator's `QUOTE_ONLY` election needs, which is the
project token into the quote — the conversion that mode promises the creator. Two requirements, two
routes, two payers.

## Guidance for interfaces

- Display the quote asset you actually read. Never relabel a stock-token entitlement as WETH.
- Never treat `PREPARED` as public launch availability.
- Never print a wrapped-native symbol you did not read from the chain profile.
- Never publish a platform address until you have read it from a source that states the code was read
  back off the chain. A predicted address and a deployed one look identical.
